'''Jean Morlet''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒɑ̃ mɔʁlɛ|lang}}; 13 January 1931 – 27 April 2007) was a French [[geophysicist]] who pioneered work in the field of [[wavelet]] analysis around the year 1975. He invented the term ''wavelet'' to describe the functions he was using. In 1981, Morlet worked with [[Alex Grossmann]] to develop what is now known as the [[Wavelet transform]].

==Biography==
Morlet studied at {{Lang|fr|[[École Polytechnique]]|italic=no}} from 1952 to 1955 and was research engineer at [[Elf Aquitaine]] when he invented wavelets to solve signal processing problems for oil prospecting.

==Awards==
He was awarded in 1997 with the Reginald Fessenden Award.<ref>{{cite web |title=SEG Awards: Reginald Fessenden |website=Virtual Geoscience Center |publisher=[[Society of Exploration Geophysicists]] |year=1997 }}</ref> He was awarded in 2001 with the first prize Prix Chéreau Lavet, from the [[French Academy of Technologies|Académie des Technologies]].

==Legacy==
The Jean-Morlet Chair at the [[Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques]] is named in his honor.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Jean-Morlet Chair|url=http://www.chairejeanmorlet.com/|website=Chaire Jean-Morlet|publisher=Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques|accessdate=9 July 2017}}</ref>
